title: Forsythoside A attenuates sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy by modulating macrophage polarization via Nrf2/NF-kappaB signaling.
authors: Sun, Yujin; Zhang, Luzheng; Qi, Xiaohui; Wang, Heng; Huang, Xi; Zhao, Lei; Xue, Song
one_liner_zh: 该文研究连翘酯苷A通过Nrf2/NF-kB信号调节巨噬细胞极化改善脓毒症心肌病，核心为炎症信号通路与心肌保护，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) is a major manifestation of sepsis-related multiple organ dysfunction, driven by uncontrolled inflammation, oxidative stress, and disrupted macrophage polarization. However, the mechanisms by which immune dysregulation contributes to myocardial injury remain incompletely understood. This study investigated whether Forsythoside A (FTA), a phenylethanoid glycoside from Forsythia suspensa, attenuates SICM by enhancing nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)-mediated inhibition of nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB), thereby reprogramming macrophage M1/M2 polarization and secondarily reducing myocardial oxidative stress and apoptosis. An LPS-induced murine model of SICM and macrophage-cardiomyocyte coculture systems were established to evaluate the cardioprotective effects of FTA. FTA significantly improved cardiac function, reduced myocardial injury, and attenuated oxidative stress and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. Mechanistically, molecular docking and transcriptomic analyses suggested the potential involvement of Nrf2-related signaling in the effects of FTA. FTA activated the Nrf2/HO-1/NQO1 antioxidant pathway while suppressing NF-kappaB activation, thereby promoting a shift in macrophage polarization from a pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Pharmacological inhibition of Nrf2 using ML385 partially reversed these protective effects. Together, these findings demonstrate that FTA alleviates SICM by modulating macrophage polarization through an Nrf2-NF-kappaB signaling axis and may represent a promising natural cardioprotective candidate.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症诱导的心肌病（SICM）是脓毒症相关多器官功能障碍的主要表现，由不受控制的炎症、氧化应激和巨噬细胞极化紊乱驱动。然而，免疫失调导致心肌损伤的机制仍未完全阐明。本研究探讨了连翘酯苷A（FTA），一种来自连翘的苯乙醇苷类化合物，是否通过增强核因子E2相关因子2（Nrf2）介导的核因子-κB（NF-κB）抑制，从而重编程巨噬细胞M1/M2极化，并继发性减轻心肌氧化应激和凋亡，来缓解SICM。建立了LPS诱导的SICM小鼠模型和巨噬细胞-心肌细胞共培养系统，以评估FTA的心脏保护作用。FTA显著改善心功能、减轻心肌损伤，并减弱氧化应激和心肌细胞凋亡。机制上，分子对接和转录组学分析提示Nrf2相关信号可能参与FTA的作用。FTA激活Nrf2/HO-1/NQO1抗氧化通路，同时抑制NF-κB激活，从而促进巨噬细胞极化从促炎性M1表型向抗炎性M2表型转变。使用ML385对Nrf2进行药理学抑制可部分逆转这些保护效应。综上，这些发现表明FTA通过Nrf2-NF-κB信号轴调节巨噬细胞极化来缓解SICM，并可能成为一种有前景的天然心脏保护候选药物。
